hypothesis: the cross-evaluator collapse excess is reproducible across independent runs, so collapse-01's +0.1994 was a property of the setup rather than one trajectory
methods:
RD="$PWD"; ROOT=""; d="$RD"; while [ "$d" != "/" ]; do [ -d "$d/src/ai_researcher" ] && { ROOT="$d"; break; }; d=$(dirname "$d"); done; [ -n "$ROOT" ] || { echo "no repo root" >&2; exit 1; }; # 5 independent runs (independent seeds) of the collapse arm; cross_excess per run is the unit of analysis, so the test is over runs
PYTHONPATH="$ROOT/src:$ROOT/demo/shared" EVO_OUT="$RD/artifacts" EVO_SEED=20261011 EVO_RUNS=5 python3 "$ROOT/demo/collapse/run_collapse_replicated.py"

kill_switch.note: the excess replicates across independent runs: extend to more judge pairings
the +0.1994 was one trajectory: record collapse-01 as an artifact of a single run, not a finding

approved_by: liuzewen (blanket 全做; sign-test endpoint, verified to survive the approve round-trip)
tension: collapse-01 reported a cross-evaluator excess of +0.1994 and was filed STOP-EXTEND, but it rests on one run of one judge pairing, and the values within a run are a trajectory whose points are not independent samples. No test can be computed from it, so the project has been citing an untestable direction-bearing arm -- one of eight. Either the excess is a property of the setup and survives independent repetition, or it is a property of one trajectory and should be struck. Nothing about a larger number of rounds within the same run can answer that, which is why the earlier arms were not merely underpowered but untestable.

power.endpoint: two-sided exact sign test over 10 independent runs (2 judge pairings x 5 seeds); a decisive split needs n>=6 at alpha=0.05
